correspondents: Sir Robert Ainslie to Peter Michell (East India Company)
shelfmark: British Library, India Office Records IOR/G/17/5 ff. 228-232
folio_note: 5 folios; catalogue calls it a "copy of cipher letter"
status: Copy for the Court of Directors; unclear whether the cipher text or the decipher is held.
why: British ambassador at the Porte writing in cipher to the East India Company about the Suez route and a Cairo agent.
access_note: BL India Office Records; not seen online
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Ottoman/Turkish sweep (research/sweep_2026-11_ottoman_turkish/); not viewed
vetting_note: Blocker stands. Third pass (6 Nov): TNA Discovery record 8b987ccd (IOR/G/17/5 ff.228-232, 'Copy of cipher letter from Sir Robert Ainslie to Peter Michell ... Read in Court 17 August 1779', digitised: false) and BL record read by curl; the catalogue summarises the letter's content in full (tribute to the Porte, a 'proper agent' at Cairo), which shows the cataloguer read a plain text, so it is not shown whether ff.228-232 hold cipher groups or the deciphered copy read to the Court. Neighbouring items in G/17/5 (f.227 covering sheet, ff.306-310 Ainslie to Michell, ff.197-199) are catalogued as ordinary letters. Searched: Ainslie/Michell 1779 Suez; Ainslie cipher 1779 secret committee/Hoskins; no printed or deciphered text found. Only the India Office reading room (BL Asian and African Studies) can settle it; no BL digitisation exists.

title: Reichshofrat Knorre: report on his conversion to Catholicism (partly in cipher) and a gift of 1,000 ducats
status: Arcinsys: "z.T. in Chiffre verfaßt". No decipherment mentioned in the description. Hanoverian Geheime Räte papers (Cal. Br. 15 K Nr. 184, about 11 leaves); the same chancery wrote decipherments between the lines in Hann. 9g (targets/mecklenburg1734), so check for that before scoring.
why: A confessional affair of a Hanoverian Reichshofrat, 1738.
score_note: Scored from the finding-aid description during the Nov 2026 German portals sweep (research/sweep_2026-11_german_portals/); not viewed
verify: Blocked (review 3 Nov 2026): Cal. Br. 15 Nr. 2225 and 2233 are not digitised, and the descriptions say only 'z.T. in Chiffre'. Blocker: a scan. Every Hanoverian chancery file viewable so far is interlined (targets/mecklenburg1734, Dep. 110 A Nr. 64 and 105), and these are the same Geheime Räte, so the description cannot support 'no decipherment'.

access_note: whether the unit is digitised is not shown in the finding-aid text; check "Digitalisate" on the unit page
vetting_note: Still no scan, and still no way to rule out interlinear decipherment. Re-fetched Arcinsys NLA HA Cal. Br. 15 Nr. 2225 (id 1680530, 'Bericht ueber den Uebertritt des Reichshofrats von Knorre zur katholischen Religion (z.T. in Chiffre verfasst)', 1738, ca. 11 Bl.) and Nr. 2233 (id 1684901, 1,000-ducat gift, 'z.T. in Chiffre', 1738-39) by curl 6 Nov 2026: both list only 'Original Akte', no Digitalisat. Four web searches (Knorre/Knoerr conversion 1738 Hannover, Geheime Raete Chiffre, Francke Halle person record for Georg Christian von Knoerr) found no edition, calendar or study of these two files and no decipherment; so no edition blocks it, but the leaf cannot be seen and the same Hanoverian Geheime Raete interlined decipherments in Hann. 9g (targets/mecklenburg1734). Unblock: NLA Hannover scan of Cal. Br. 15 Nr. 2225 (about 11 leaves) to see whether the cipher passages carry a decipherment.
